- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward that average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ sentiment-weighted price changes.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture volatility; increase forecast variance by ±1–2% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
